evidence: NESTING ARITHMETIC (static, passes). Frozen task.toml: [agent] timeout_sec = 7200.0, [environment] build_timeout_sec = 600.0, [verifier] timeout_sec = 13200.0 - identical to the template and staged-task-contract.md lines 54/57/63 (template-vs-task diff of task.toml differs only in identity/metadata lines). test.sh is byte-identical to the template and runs `timeout "$budget_sec" rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (lines 203-210), so dimensions within a suite run sequentially. Gates `run_suite gates 1500` (line 213): render timeout 600 + constraints timeout 600 = 1200 < 1500. Scored `run_suite scored 11100` (line 224): functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 < 11100. Gates 1500 + scored 11100 = 12600 < verifier 13200, leaving 600 s for copy/launch/liveness/score.py. Judge timeouts equal the template values (600/600/9000/900/900). LIVENESS: test.sh lines 115-125 poll probe_ready 120 x 0.25 s (~30 s nominal; urlopen timeout=2 per URL, pathological worst case ~510 s, still inside the 600 s slack). Restart helper: kill wait 50 x 0.1 s + the same ready loop (~35 s nominal) < restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 (line 11). BUILD: environment/Dockerfile is node:22-bookworm-slim + small apt + npm -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1; 600 s is plausible but no measured cold-build time was supplied. FIT TO WORKLOAD (unmeasured, the risk): the functional dimension is ONE batched claude-code session (judge.toml mode = "batched", timeout = 9000) with 44 criteria (counted [[criterion]] blocks; template has 2) and a protocol at functional/prompt.md lines 25-51 (Z, S, M, L, C, B with 15 numbered sub-steps, N, T, U, K, R, V, A, D) requiring ~10 independent browser contexts (10 'independent context' occurrences), at least 7 named accounts, many captured-request replays (R alone: 7 replays each for Aud and Tomas plus 10 anonymous replays), several 15-second live-arrival waits (U, V), and a final restart. Under z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx through Playwright MCP, a plausible several-hundred-tool-call walk is in the same order of magnitude as 9000 s, so the budget may or may not cover the golden. raw-evidence-index.json states: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent', and each entry is 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'; results/workspace.json has no total-duration field. With no measured full configured judge duration, SKILL.md ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY.md ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number') forbid passing the 'long enough' half. Positives: no task-local timeout change (budgets untouched, as the policy requires absent a measured reason), nesting correct, and functional prompt line 53 maps budget exhaustion to 'NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation' instead of an observed app failure.
counterexample: Conforming app that could fail: a fully correct implementation forces the judge down every successful path (all S/M/L/B sub-steps, T/U waits, A audit, D restart). If the single batched functional session exhausts 9000 s, the late protocols (A Activity, D restart -> hro_restart, possibly V/R) go unobserved and score 0 per prompt line 53, or the batched dimension returns no parsed result, giving functional 0, failing the 0.05 floor and reward 0. Broken app that could do relatively better: an app that refuses or fails early shortens the walk, so the judge reaches late protocols within budget; the richer correct app is more exposed to timeout than a weak one, risking ranking inversion. Not demonstrated - no configured judge run was measured - so this is an unresolved risk, not a confirmed defect.
suggested_fix: Measure a full configured verifier run (gates + scored with claude-code / z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx) on the golden and record functional judge wall time and whether every protocol through D was reached; if it nears 9000 s, cut redundant protocol steps/replays (with matching public-scope changes) or, with explicit recorded authorization below five hours, narrowly adjust the functional judge timeout and scored/verifier budgets while preserving nesting.
